newsitem.title: USA: Collins sells unit to Safety Comp.
newsitem.headline: Collins sells unit to Safety Comp.

text.p: Collins & Aikman Corp said Tuesday it agreed to sell its air restraint and technical products division to Safety Components International Inc for $56.3 million in cash.
The supplier of car interior systems said it expected to close the deal within 60 to 90 days. It added it will use the proceeds to reduce long-term debt.
Safety Components said it expects to issue $80 million in 10-year senior subordinated debt securities to pay for the acquisition.

Safety Components said it would assume under $1 million in existing debt in the form of capitalized leases in addition to the $56.3 million cash purchase price. It added it is negotiating to buy a 350,000 square-feet building next to the division's plant in Greenville, S.C., for about $1.25 million.

The manufacturer of car airbags said it expected the acquisition to add more than $80 million in annual revenues in the first year of operations, resulting in total annual revenues of more than $200 million.
"All we're saying now is the acquisition will be accretive to earnings in the first year of operations," said chief financial officer Jeffrey Kaplan, who declined to elaborate.
Safety Components posted a $425,000 profit on revenues of $24.2 million in the quarter ended March 31, compared with a $1.2 million profit on $21.5 million in sales the year before.
Trading in the company's stock was halted and then resumed on Nasdaq Tuesday morning. The first sale after the resumption was at 10-47/64, up 47/64 over Monday's close.
For Collins & Aikman, the division's spin-off is the latest in a series.
The company agreed to sell its Mastercraft Group unit to privately-held Joan Fabrics Corp for $310 million on April 25. Just like now, it said it would use the proceeds to reduce long-term debt.

On February 6 it said it sold its floor coverings business for $195 million to a company formed by Virginia merchant banking firm Quad-C Inc and Paribas Principal Partners, the U.S. private equity unit of Cie Financiere de Paribas.
With every spin-off, the company said it would "focus on its core automotive interior trim operations."

The company reported a net income of $97.5 million, or $1.43 a share, in the first quarter, compared with $136.4 million, or $1.95 a share, the year before. Its stock traded at 10-3/8 Monday morning, up 3/8.
